mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute the ratio of shots-FOR to possession-FOR for TEAM_A across ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 windows; do the same for TEAM_B. Test whether the joint recent-vs-longrun shift in both observables simultaneously (possession up, shots up) reflects a stable or changing shots-per-possession rate, conditioning on both observables together rather than either alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent possession share rises substantially above its long-run mean, its shots-per-possession rate is expected to either rise with it (compounding effect) or saturate/decline (diminishing returns); the direction of this joint shift is what the engine should measure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent possession share has surged dramatically relative to its long-run average, while its recent shot volume has also risen sharply. The joint relationship between a team's possession-to-shots conversion efficiency (shots produced per unit of possession held) in recent form versus its long-run baseline reveals whether the recent possession gain is translating into proportionally more shots, or whether the conversion rate is saturating or diverging.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint ratio of two distinct observables (shots and possession) across two time windows simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band — it is a cross-observable rate that must be computed jointly.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute shots_on_target / shots across ALL_PRIOR and RECENT_5 windows. Test whether the recent increase in shot volume (both teams show higher recent shots) is accompanied by a proportional, improving, or degrading on-target rate — conditioning on both observables jointly, not either in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: A team whose shot volume rises sharply in recent form is expected to show either a stable, rising, or declining on-target rate; the direction of this joint shift (volume × precision) is the testable relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between a team's shots volume and its shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target / shots) captures shooting precision. When both teams show recent surges in shot volume, the team whose on-target rate holds up or improves under higher shot loads is structurally different from one whose precision degrades. This cross-observable joint relationship between shot volume and on-target conversion is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint ratio across two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) compared across time windows. Neither observable alone, nor either compared to a single opponent-descriptor band, captures the precision-under-volume dynamic.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on TEAM_A's first-half vs second-half goals-FOR and goals-AGAINST rates alongside TEAM_B's first-half vs second-half goals-FOR and goals-AGAINST rates. The interaction of TEAM_A's second-half scoring tendency with TEAM_B's first-half conceding tendency (and vice versa) is the joint conditioning, not either team's half-split alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team is structurally a second-half scorer and the opponent is structurally a first-half conceder, the combined match goal-timing distribution is expected to be more concentrated in specific halves than either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The two teams show asymmetric within-match goal-scoring distributions across halves. TEAM_A scores and concedes more in the second half than the first, while TEAM_B concedes more in the first half than the second. The joint conditioning on both teams' half-level goal distributions simultaneously — rather than either team's half split in isolation — reveals whether the match's goal-timing profile is structurally skewed by the interaction of these asymmetries.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (each team's half-level goal distribution) and their interaction. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or recent/longrun split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of cards_2h-FOR to fouls-FOR (all-prior). Then compare this ratio between the two teams and against the competition context. Test whether a team with a higher foul rate also shows a proportionally higher or disproportionately higher second-half card rate — i.e., whether the foul-to-card conversion in the second half is linear or exhibits a threshold/saturation pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: A team with a higher foul rate is expected to show a rising second-half card rate, but the rate of increase in cards per foul may saturate or accelerate beyond a foul-rate threshold, rather than scaling linearly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) is jointly related to foul production rates. A team that commits many fouls overall but whose second-half card rate is disproportionately high relative to its foul rate suggests a non-linear threshold effect — card issuance per foul rises in the second half beyond what foul volume alone predicts. The joint relationship between fouls-FOR and cards_2h-FOR, compared across both teams, is the mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint cross-observable relationship (fouls × cards_2h) with a within-match period dimension (second half only for cards), requiring two distinct observables to be related to each other. It is not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession-FOR rate and the opponent's offsides-FOR rate (which equals the team's offsides-AGAINST). Test whether the team with higher possession (TEAM_B) is associated with fewer opponent offside attempts, and whether TEAM_A's higher offside rate co-occurs with lower possession — examining the cross-team asymmetry in this joint relationship.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: A team with higher possession is expected to suppress opponent offside attempts (opponent offsides-FOR falls as possession-AGAINST rises), while a lower-possession team pressing higher up the pitch is expected to generate more offsides; the asymmetry between the two teams in this joint possession-offside relationship is the testable direction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: TEAM_A generates substantially more offsides than TEAM_B (both for and against), while TEAM_B holds more possession. The joint relationship between a team's possession share and the offsides it draws from the opponent (offsides-AGAINST) captures whether high-possession teams suppress opponent offside attempts — i.e., whether possession dominance and opponent offside rate are inversely related across these two teams in a way that is asymmetric between them.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (possession and offsides) measured asymmetrically across the two teams simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band, and the cross-team asymmetric joint relationship is structurally richer than any covered class.
